messages:
tom-acme: Hey team — after the model flip last night our production parser started crashing. Looks like some responses are now wrapped in a top-level "payload" object instead of the expected schema. Example (from a failing request):
```json
{
  "payload": {
    "order_id": 12345,
    "items": [{"sku": "X1", "qty": 2}]
  }
}
```
This breaks our downstream deserializer which expects root-level "order_id" and "items". Happened starting ~2024-07-29T03:42:00Z. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d. Any ideas?

sara-cs: Thanks for the ping, Tom. Is it every response or intermittent? Can you paste the raw response for a request that succeeded and one that failed? Also which model/endpoint you were hitting?

 tom-acme: It's intermittent — about 1 in 8 responses. Here is a successful one:
```json
{
  "order_id": 12346,
  "items": [{"sku": "Y2", "qty": 1}]
}
```
and another failed: 
```json
{
  "payload": {
    "order_id": 12347,
    "items": []
  },
  "meta": {"duration_ms": 42}
}
```
We call the hosted API at POST /v1/generate with model=redwood-served-v3.3 and prompt containing our JSON template.

 raj-eng: @sara-cs tagging infra/ML: can you confirm which model variant rolled and if any prompt templating change was deployed? That intermittent rate suggests branching by template or a new system-level wrapper.

 deploy-bot: Deployed redwood-served-v3.3 -> redwood-served-v3.4 at 2024-07-29T03:40:12Z by deploy_user. Change summary: "prompt-templating refactor; optional output namespacing flag added".

 alisa-ml: That matches. We introduced an optional namespacing step to avoid collisions for some customers; default was supposed to be false but there's a bug in feature-flag evaluation for some tenant metadata keys. Could cause intermittent wrapping.

 sara-cs: Ok — filing internal ticket and escalating. @tom-acme, quick question: can you tolerate a compatibility fix on our side (strip top-level "payload" when present) while we roll back the flag?

 tom-acme: Yes please — that would unblock us immediately. ETA?

 ben-oncall: We can push a fast runtime-middleware patch that strips a single top-level "payload" wrapper for specific customer IDs. Will need a small config change + hot-restart on the inference edge. Estimated 3-4 hours if approved.

 raj-eng: Short-term plan: apply middleware for customer acme-corp to unwrap payload. Medium-term: fix feature-flag evaluation and add unit tests. Also add a schema conformance guard to log and optionally reject wrapped responses.

 sara-cs: Filing an incident ticket with priority P2, will notify legal/CS if this causes SLA tests to fail. Tom, we'll DM you a temporary header to opt your requests into the compatibility middleware so it only affects your traffic.

 tom-acme: Thanks, Sara. We'll add the header as soon as you send it. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

 alisa-ml: For root cause notes: the templating refactor introduced an optional `namespaced_output` parameter. Due to a parsing bug it was being set true when tenant metadata contained a legacy `team_namespace` key. Patch in progress.

 ben-oncall: Patching runtime now; will post update when hot-restart completes.

 deploy-bot: Hot-restart on edges started at 2024-07-29T07:15:02Z for acme-corp middleware rollout.

 sara-cs: Update: customer confirmed parser is green after middleware. Rolling back the feature-flag change to default-false in next deploy; follow-up postmortem planned. :white_check_mark:

 tom-acme: Confirmed — errors dropped to zero after adding the header. Thanks everyone.

 raj-eng: Follow-ups: add a canary test that validates JSON schema conformance for 1000 requests post-deploy, and add an alert if >0.5% responses contain unexpected top-level keys.

 sara-cs: Will include in postmortem action items. Closing thread but keeping ticket open until rollback done. :eyes:
